theory.overview: Computational Geometry deals with algorithms for geometric objects: points, lines, polygons, convex hulls. It's essential for computer graphics, robotics, GIS, and CAD systems. Key techniques include sweep line algorithms, divide and conquer, and geometric data structures. Common problems include finding convex hulls, detecting line intersections, closest pair of points, and point-in-polygon tests.

keyConcepts.name: Convex Hull
keyConcepts.description: Smallest convex polygon containing all points. Graham Scan O(n log n), Jarvis March O(nh), Monotone Chain O(n log n).

keyConcepts.name: Line Sweep
keyConcepts.description: Imaginary line sweeps across plane, tracking active events. Used for intersection detection and Voronoi diagrams.

keyConcepts.name: Orientation Test
keyConcepts.description: Cross product determines if three points make clockwise/counter-clockwise turn. Foundation for many algorithms.

keyConcepts.name: Point in Polygon
keyConcepts.description: Ray casting: cast horizontal ray from point, count intersections with polygon edges. Odd = inside, even = outside.

complexity.lineIntersection: O((n + k) log n) where k = intersections
complexity.pointInPolygon: O(n) or O(log n) for convex

algorithmSteps.description: 8 points for convex hull. Find smallest convex polygon containing all.
Sort points by x-coordinate (tie-break by y).
Build lower hull: Keep while making counter-clockwise turns.
Build upper hull: Process in reverse x order.
Combine lower and upper hulls (excluding last point of each to avoid duplication).
Convex hull has 5 vertices. Area = 9 square units.

minigame.title: Convex Hull Builder
